body: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work-list","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"facets":{},"total-results":2773475,"items":[{"abstract":"Replay-free class-incremental vibration diagnosis must incorporate new fault categories after deployment while retaining earlier decisions without storing old signals. Sequential optimization is difficult in this setting because it can distort both individual class representatives and their relative geometry, especially when vibration patterns also vary with operating conditions. We introduce graph continual prototype learning (GCPL), which represents each observed class by a prototype and connects related prototypes through a sparse feature-space graph. New-class samples initialize new nodes and local edges, whereas node- and edge-stability terms constrain changes to the previously learned class structure. The graph is learned from embeddings rather than predefined fault taxonomies, and its retained state scales with the number of classes instead of the number of vibration windows. A leakage-resistant evaluation protocol is specified for four public bearing datasets and jointly measures cumulative-class accuracy, old-class forgetting, new-class learning, and robustness to operating-condition shifts. This formulation provides a compact pattern-recognition framework for studying relational structure in replay-free incremental diagnosis.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2139\/ssrn.7230759","type":"posted-content","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Graph continual prototype learning for replay-free class-incremental vibration diagnosis"],"author":[{"given":"qinao","family":"hu","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.2139\/ssrn.7230759"},{"abstract":"Intelligent condition-monitoring systems must often incorporate fault categories that appear after deployment, while retaining historical vibration records may be restricted by storage, privacy, or maintenance constraints. This paper addresses the resulting replay-free class-incremental vibration fault diagnosis problem. We propose graph continual prototype learning (GCPL), a compact AI-based diagnostic framework that stores class prototypes, diagonal dispersion estimates, and a sparse relation graph instead of previous signal windows. New classes are inserted locally, while prototype anchoring, old-edge consistency, neighborhood-rank preservation, reliability weighting, and a topology-aware boundary margin constrain destabilization of the retained class structure. Record- or bearing-level splits are applied before windowing on CWRU, Paderborn, XJTU-SY, and JNU to avoid overlapping-window leakage. Across four datasets and five matched seeds, GCPL attains AIA values of 95.1%, 91.2%, 89.5%, and 92.4%, improving on the strongest replay-free baseline by 2.1\u20132.6 points and reducing final-session forgetting by 1.8\u20132.3 points. Additional tests cover relation drift, operating-condition shift, additive noise, low-shot and long-tail increments, class order, calibration, and retained-state efficiency. Predictive models must safely adapt to incoming patient data. In this paper, we introduce Balanced-Reservoir Replay (BRR), a simple modification to reservoir sampling that preserves minority-class examples when the buffer is full. We evaluated BRR on the eICU-CRD dataset (2,520 patients, 8.37% mortality) using only age and gender, in a task-incremental setup with eight tasks and buffer sizes ranging from 0 to 1000 samples.Using a 1000-sample buffer (~\u200940% of past data), BRR outperformed standard sequential training, achieving an average AUC of 0.628\u2009\u00b1\u20090.019 compared to 0.610\u2009\u00b1\u20090.016 (p\u2009<\u20090.01). It also reduced forgetting by 16% (0.106\u2009\u00b1\u20090.047 vs. 0.126\u2009\u00b1\u20090.066), which narrowed the gap with cumulative training by 39%. A clinical composite score, which penalized forgetting twice as much as accuracy gains (\u03bb\u2009=\u20092.0), indicated that a buffer size of 1000 was optimal. We conducted a sensitivity analysis of eight configurations of training duration (40 vs. 80 epochs per task) and forgetting penalties (\u03bb\u2009=\u20090.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0) supported the validity of this selection.This work questions the idea of minimal memory in continual learning. It indicates that retaining some past data can improve accuracy, enhance stability, and help meet regulatory requirements for slowly changing, low-data clinical tasks. BRR only needs about 50 KB of data, and it\u2019s easy to understand and use in places where resources are limited. r\u00e9seaux de neurones profonds<\/jats:title>\n <jats:p xml:lang=\"fr\">Nous nous int\u00e9ressons au probl\u00e8me de l'apprentissage continu de r\u00e9seaux de neurones artificiels dans le cas o\u00f9 les donn\u00e9es ne sont accessibles que pour une seule cat\u00e9gorie \u00e0 la fois. Pour rem\u00e9dier au probl\u00e8me de l'oubli catastrophique qui limite les performances d'apprentissage dans ces conditions, nous proposons une approche bas\u00e9e sur la repr\u00e9sentation des donn\u00e9es d'une cat\u00e9gorie par une loi normale. Les transformations associ\u00e9es \u00e0 ces repr\u00e9sentations sont effectu\u00e9es \u00e0 l'aide de r\u00e9seaux inversibles, qui peuvent alors \u00eatre entra\u00een\u00e9s avec les donn\u00e9es d'une seule cat\u00e9gorie. Chaque cat\u00e9gorie se voit attribuer un r\u00e9seau pour repr\u00e9senter ses caract\u00e9ristiques. Pr\u00e9dire la cat\u00e9gorie revient alors \u00e0 identifier le r\u00e9seau le plus repr\u00e9sentatif. L'avantage d'une telle approche est qu'une fois qu'un r\u00e9seau est entra\u00een\u00e9, il n'est plus n\u00e9cessaire de le mettre \u00e0 jour par la suite, chaque r\u00e9seau \u00e9tant ind\u00e9pendant des autres. C'est cette propri\u00e9t\u00e9 particuli\u00e8rement avantageuse qui d\u00e9marque notre m\u00e9thode des pr\u00e9c\u00e9dents travaux dans ce domaine. Nous appuyons notre d\u00e9monstration sur des exp\u00e9riences r\u00e9alis\u00e9es sur divers jeux de donn\u00e9es et montrons que notre approche fonctionne favorablement compar\u00e9 \u00e0 l'\u00e9tat de l'art. Dans un second temps, nous proposons d'optimiser notre approche en r\u00e9duisant son impact en m\u00e9moire en factorisant les param\u00e8tres des r\u00e9seaux. Il est alors possible de r\u00e9duire significativement le co\u00fbt de stockage de ces r\u00e9seaux avec une perte de performances limit\u00e9e. Esteemed as a fundamental goal in artificial intelligence, continual learning grapples with an enduring challenge—catastrophic forgetting. A proficient model must exhibit adaptability for new data assimilation and robustness to retain existing knowledge. Class-incremental learning (CIL) aids the gradual integration of knowledge from newly introduced classes, forming a universal classifier. However, directly training the model with fresh class instances triggers a problem—forgetting distinguishing features of prior classes, causing a performance decline.
